clue.text: Item for kitchen goes with mine

parts.note: goes in the sense of takes a turn, as in 'whose turn is it?' — 'turns'
a mine is a pit dug for coal or ore

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that comes as a set with a mine, like some odd catalogue pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' is a noun here, as in someone having goes or turns at a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit is a rotating spit, or the device turning it, used for roasting meat by a kitchen fire.

clue.text: Figure rising crime is court's raison d'être

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the crime word is reversed

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime

explanation.surface: A rising crime figure is what the courts exist to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis court exists so that the game can be played on it: the sport is its whole purpose.

clue.text: No longer cultivate a lot of wit, following soldiers

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the wit is placed after the soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, famous wit

explanation.surface: Giving up cultivating a sense of humour after joining the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers come first because the wit is 'following' them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewild land is to stop farming it and let it return to its natural uncultivated state.

clue.text: Small club overrunning eg Chelsea, one doing lots of pressing

indicators.note: overrunning means spreading over, so the small club wraps around the team

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an iron is a type of golf club
Chelsea is a London football team

explanation.surface: A minor football club overwhelming Chelsea, a side that presses a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' is a football tactic in the surface, but means ironing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron is a household appliance used for pressing creases out of clothes.

clue.text: Stifling short satisfied sound, wearing attractive outfit for dogging?

parts.note: wearing something means being in it

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the attractive outfit wraps round the sound

parts.note: hot means sexually attractive
a suit is an outfit of clothes

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter

parts.note: a purr is the contented sound of a cat

explanation.surface: A sexy outfit muffling a contented little noise, with a saucy hint at dogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogging' has a seamy slang sense, but here it means following someone closely, as a dog does.
explanation.definitionFit: In hot pursuit means chasing closely behind, which is what dogging someone's footsteps involves.

clue.text: Plain idiot with plan to retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the pair of words is read from right to left

parts.note: a sap is a fool
a map is a plan of an area

explanation.surface: A fool with a scheme is told to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading SAP MAP backwards gives the answer in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grassland plains of South America, especially Argentina.

clue.text: Not everyone should hear this song

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a remark said quietly so that only some of those present catch it
second meaning: the A-side, the main song on a single record

explanation.walkthrough: An aside is the actor's remark to the audience that other characters are not meant to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre an aside is a confidential remark; on a vinyl single the A-side carries the lead track.

clue.text: Act I put on, a divine fellow in the main

definitions.text: a divine fellow in the main

parts.note: to pose is to put on an act, to pretend
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: An actor in a play's first act as a godlike character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea, a deity whose domain is the ocean.

clue.text: Get rid of starter of salt fish no longer on the menu

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so take the first letter of salt

parts.note: hake is a sea fish
a dish that is off is no longer available

explanation.surface: A restaurant has dropped its salt fish starter from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a menu course, matching 'menu', but it just picks a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake off a cold or a pursuer is to get free of it, to be rid of it.

clue.text: City backing shop that's picked up capital

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the city word is turned round

parts.note: a wen is an old word for a large crowded city, from Cobbett's 'Great Wen' for London

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the shop word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: A City firm supporting a shop that has attracted investment capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City backing' looks like financial support from London's Square Mile. The old word for a city comes from Cobbett, who called London 'the Great Wen'.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital city of India, seat of its national government.

clue.text: Break Sierra and another car that won't start?

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a car that won't start, punningly, has lost its first letter

parts.note: the Ford Fiesta, another Ford model like the Sierra

explanation.surface: A breakdown story: a Ford Sierra and a second car that refuses to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' looks like the Ford car, matching 'another car', but here it only gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a short afternoon nap or rest, a break from the day's work.

clue.text: Where to write about horny male running amok

indicators.note: about means around, so the writing place surrounds the male

parts.note: you write on the page
a ram is a male sheep, which has horns

explanation.surface: Instructions on where to write about a lustful man going wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' is literal, having horns, not the slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: On the rampage means behaving violently and out of control, like running amok.

clue.text: African nation in recession clings to singular belief

indicators.note: the reversed nation holds on to a letter in its middle
receding means going backwards, so the nation's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: An African country in an economic slump holds onto one belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recession' reads like economics but signals a reversal, giving ILAM, which then holds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic religious faith founded on the teachings of the prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Fruit or nettle with spike around it

indicators.note: the spike word goes around the nettle word, enclosing it

parts.note: a tine is a prong or spike, as on a fork or antler
to nettle is to annoy, and anger is the verb in the same sense

explanation.surface: Choosing between a piece of fruit or a nettle wrapped round a spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettle' looks like the plant, but it is the verb meaning irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small sweet citrus fruit related to the mandarin orange.

clue.text: Resisting current rough work, we hear, by old boring academic

indicators.note: we hear means the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: a draft is a rough first version of a piece of work

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the old letter goes inside the academic

parts.note: prof is short for professor

explanation.surface: A dull old academic produces rough work that, apparently, resists the trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like current affairs but is a current of air, a draught.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtproof windows or doors are sealed so that cold air currents cannot get through.

clue.text: Emperor, say, spread guards round part of camp

indicators.note: guards means encloses protectively, so the spread surrounds the rest

parts.note: pâté is a savoury paste spread on bread
O is round in shape
a tent is one unit of a campsite

explanation.surface: An emperor's troops fanning out to defend part of a military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb describing the guards, but it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or ruler, and an emperor is one example of such a powerful sovereign.

clue.text: Pervert isn't commonly getting slap

parts.note: to warp something is to twist or pervert it
ain't is a nonstandard, colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A deviant is not usually given a slap in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap' is slang for theatrical make-up, as is war paint.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is informal for heavy cosmetics, and slap is British slang for make-up.

clue.text: Big reputation? Artist consequently loses head

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: hence means therefore, consequently

explanation.surface: A famous artist's reputation, and as a result someone gets the chop.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as loose: eminence is high standing or fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence means distinction and fame, a high standing in public esteem.

clue.text: Notice tiny country in which Republican is to run

parts.note: an ad is a notice advertising something
mini means very small

indicators.note: the Republican letter sits inside the country word

parts.note: a state is a nation or country
R is the US abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An announcement that a Republican is to stand for office in some small country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like running for election in the surface, but it means manage.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to manage or direct the affairs of an organisation, i.e. to run it.

clue.text: Get back ruler overthrown by power grab

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the ruler's letters are reversed

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a coup is a sudden seizure of power

explanation.surface: A monarch toppled in a seizure of power, trying to regain the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup losses is to recover or regain them.

clue.text: Tunesmith's numbers filling holiday season up

indicators.note: the numbers fill the middle of the reversed season
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the season is reversed

parts.note: Noel is Christmas
N is short for number, so NN is numbers

explanation.surface: A songwriter's tracks fill the festive airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed season is LEON, with NN placed inside to make LE-NN-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lennon wrote many of the Beatles' songs, so he was a composer, a writer of tunes.

clue.text: Criticise those people constricting one's faith

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: constricting means squeezing round, so the people word encloses the other

parts.note: them refers to those people
one is I, and 's is short for is, so one's is I + S

explanation.surface: Attacking a group for restricting someone's religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' looks possessive, but read it as 'one is', giving I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is the religious belief that God is identical with the universe and nature.

clue.text: Not half elated on daughter getting engaged

indicators.note: only half of the word, its first two letters, is used

parts.note: high means elated, in very good spirits
re means on, concerning
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent thrilled, 'not half', at their daughter's engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it means 'only half'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hired is to be taken on, engaged for a job.

clue.text: How tale ends in delightful relation

indicators.note: in places the end letter inside the delightful word

parts.note: nice means pleasant, delightful

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so take the last of tale

explanation.surface: How a story finishes in a lovely relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is a link word introducing the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family relation: the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Give a wide berth to high region

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated or out of sorts, so the letters of the next word are muddled

explanation.surface: Advice to steer well clear of some mountainous area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like it describes a highland region, but it signals rearranging REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to pay no attention to them, to avoid or shun them.

clue.text: Bickie and a doughnut separately scoffed by Gallic bigwig

indicators.note: the two letters are put into the name at different places, not together
scoffed means eaten, so the bigwig takes the letter into his mouth

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is President of France
a doughnut is ring-shaped, like the letter O

explanation.surface: The French president wolfs down a biscuit and a doughnut one after the other.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes in after MAC and O after MACAR, making MACARO-ON. 'Bickie' is informal British/Australian for biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small sweet biscuit made with ground almonds or coconut and egg white.

clue.text: Outside of tweedy coats tear with it

indicators.note: coats means covers round, so the outside letters wrap the tear word
the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: A tweed jacket's exterior gets ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' is the verb rhyming with 'bear', not a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy and 'with it' are both informal ways of saying fashionable and up to date.

clue.text: Darling ally's safe with cooking equipment

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A sweetheart's friend keeps a safe alongside the pots and pans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is the family in Barrie's story (Wendy Darling and her brothers), not a term of endearment; the capital at the start of the clue hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan befriends and leads the Darling children to Neverland in J M Barrie's play.
